tier_rationale: No radio: the manufacturer's own product page describes only a battery-powered dial/digital timer with no Bluetooth, WiFi, or app, and Orbit's FCC grantee record (ML6) — which includes dozens of grants for its B-hyve Bluetooth and WiFi timer lines — has no entry for model 62061.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes, because nothing was ever connected. The 62061 is a battery-powered valve with a digital display: you set runtime and interval on the unit itself, and it retains the program through battery changes. There is no B-hyve app pairing step for this model and no account anywhere in its operation.

repairability.notes: Sold as a sealed battery-powered unit; Orbit does not list field-replaceable internal parts beyond the AA batteries. Low cost makes whole-unit replacement the practical repair path.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: no Bluetooth/WiFi/app/cloud mentioned; runs on 2 AA batteries with program retained during battery changes; runtime 1-240 minutes, interval every 6/12 hours or 1-7 days, rain delay 1-3 days, current price $36.99.

FCC grantee list for Orbit Irrigation Product Inc. (grantee code ML6), 45 entries spanning 1996-2025: extensive wireless grants for the B-hyve Bluetooth hose timer line (HT31BT/HT32BT/HT34BT), B-hyve WiFi indoor/outdoor timers (WT24E/WT25E/WT26), and gateway/RF controllers — establishing Orbit files grants when a timer has a radio. No grant found for model 62061 or 62061N.

open_questions: Orbit sells a visually similar 'B-hyve' branded hose timer line (Bluetooth/WiFi) alongside this plain-dial 62061 — a buyer should check for the B-hyve name/logo on the box, since the two share shelf space at the same retailers.
notes: Sprinkler and hose timers are a category where the manufacturer sells the exact same physical form factor — a battery-powered inline valve with a small digital display — in both a no-radio version and a Bluetooth/WiFi 'B-hyve' version. The 62061 is the plain one.
